A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable algorithms, tables, mathematical statements, proofs and appendices. Material moved into v3's appendices can be matched reliably to v2.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical algorithms, impossibility constructions and proofs, without original experimental, simulation or data-analysis results in the main text or appendices.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical throughout. Its new Example 5.2 illustrates the construction of a picking sequence; it is not an empirical study.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–3, the frequency-prediction reduction and the noisy-advice procedures retain their steps. Revised explanations and Example 5.2 do not introduce a procedural change.

E1.justification: Neither version uses empirical training or evaluation datasets. The added illustrative example remains within the existing frequency-prediction setting.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline comparisons. The theoretical comparison with Zhou et al. (2023), including the six-good counterexample to its PROP1 guarantee, is retained.

E3.justification: Neither PDF contains experimental evaluation protocols, data splits, training budgets or testing procedures. No such settings are added in v3.

E4.justification: The noisy-prediction analyses and existing counterexamples are retained, including v2 Example B.1 as v3 Example C.1. New Example 5.2 explains the existing construction rather than adding an ablation, robustness test or substantive case analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The prediction-error parameters describe deterministic theoretical guarantees, not statistical uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the theoretical guarantees retain their values, including the 3/4 + 3/3836 MMS bound with frequency predictions and the tight (sqrt(5)-1)/2 EFX bound for two identical agents with normalization information. No empirical result entries are added.

T1.justification: The assumptions, bounds and proof arguments are preserved after relocation and renumbering, including v2 Theorem 5.7 as v3 Theorem 5.6 and Theorem 6.3 as Theorem E.3. Appendix D.1 explicitly writes the standard earthmover formula for the matching-cost concept already described in v2; it does not change the guarantee or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same scope: impossibilities without information, normalization-based EF1/PROP1 guarantees, transfer of offline shares using frequency predictions, and noisy-advice guarantees. The main scientific claims are not strengthened or narrowed.

C2.justification: v3 adds explicit explanations of why share guarantees do not settle pairwise EF1, why the two-agent restrictions are structural, and why extending positive results beyond additive valuations requires new ideas. The conclusion also removes unequal entitlements as a future-work direction.

D1.justification: The O(mn) implementation of Algorithm 1, O(m^2 n) implementation of Algorithm 2 and O(log m) per-agent matching rule are retained, with some details relocated to Appendix D. No code, data-access or hardware information changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds a prophet-inequality comparison citing Correa et al. (2019), adds Teh (2026), and expands the distinction from bandit-learning models. It removes the repeated-allocation discussion and peripheral references accompanying future directions, while retaining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 extensively reorganizes the narrative: most proofs move to Appendices B–D, the detailed identical-valuation treatment moves to Appendix E, and explanatory summaries and Example 5.2 support the condensed main text. It also introduces incorrect theorem references in Section 5 and an unresolved reference in Lemma D.2.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes a two-column main text and bibliography with new typography and running headers, followed by single-column appendices. Table 1 is reformatted and relocated, Algorithm 1 becomes column-width, and Algorithms 2–3 and the valuation tables move into appendices without new result displays.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies Algorithm 1's removal condition, adds an accessible ordered-instance example, makes matching-cost notation explicit and explains applicability limits while preserving the proofs. These modest clarity gains are partially offset by the mistaken reference to Theorem 5.4 as the share theorem and the unresolved '?? 30' reference in Lemma D.2.
